title.narrative: Fujian Coastal Cities Climate-Resilient Development and Biodiversity Conservation Project

description.narrative:
The proposed project in coastal province of Fujian in the PRC will address the significant climate change risks and hazards, and biodiversity loss challenges of two coastal cities. Project objectives will be to improve urban climate change resilience and biodiversity of two cities in coastal province of Fujian in the PRC. Lessons and potential replication will benefit also other coastal cities in Fujian Province and the PRC through a strategic knowledge partnership between the two cities, the province and the national government. Three outputs are proposed.
Output 1: Capacity of institutions for coastal climate and biodiversity action enhanced. This output will strengthen capacity of institutions and interagency coordination on risk-informed and gender-responsive climate and biodiversity conservation actions. This includes consulting services and investments in ICT platforms for shared monitoring and cross-agency coordination for urban resilience, early warning and biodiversity monitoring.
Output 2: Coastal cities resilience green and gray infrastructure and facilities improved. This output includes structural and non-structural measures, including green and gray flood risk management infrastructure, an emergency response center, and related digitalization equipment and cross-sector ICT platforms.
Output 3: Biodiversity conservation and enhancement measures in coastal wetlands and mangroves implemented. This output includes conservation of wetlands and mangroves in national nature reserves, and biodiversity habitat expansion through wetland and mangroves restoration and change to sustainable agriculture and aquaculture practices in buffer and experimental zones to the protected areas.

description.narrative: Climate change resilience and biodiversity in Fuzhou and Yunxiao enhanced

At least 100 project staff (including at least 30 women) (Fuzhou: 50, of which 15 are women; Yunxiao: 50, of which 15 are women) applied new knowledge and skills on resilience and biodiversity planning and operations Data Source: Surveys of staff in Fuzhou and Yunxiao administrative departments engaged in project implementation, operation, and management Actual value:

At least 221 ha of intertidal wetland areas (Fuzhou: 154 ha, Yunxiao: 67 ha) and 7 ha mangroves restored and under improved management (Yunxiao), and at least 630 ha transformed into ecological aquaculture and farmland (Fuzhou: 130 ha, Yunxiao: 500 ha) Data Source: Annual project progress reports and completion reports of executing agencies Actual value:

At least 4.4 million people (Fuzhou: 4.1 million, Yunxiao: 0.3 million) in project areas (of which 2.1 million are women; Fuzhou: 2.0 million, Yunxiao: 0.1 million) benefited from improved resilience infrastructure and ecosystem services, and reduced flood risk and urban heat Data Source: Annual project progress reports and completion reports of executing agencies Actual value:
Output/s as listed by the project staff.
